concepts.title: Coordinate Axes and Coordinate Planes in Space
concepts.definition: To locate points off the flat page, three mutually perpendicular number lines are set up meeting at an origin: the x-axis, y-axis and z-axis. Each pair of axes spans a flat coordinate plane -- the XY, YZ and ZX planes -- and together the three axes cut all of space into eight octants.
concepts.key_idea: Three axes give three coordinate planes, and the trio of planes partitions space into eight octants numbered by sign pattern.
concepts.textbook_ref: kemh111.txt lines 40-110 (section 11.2, coordinate axes, three coordinate planes, eight octants)

solution_steps.explain: The x, y and z-axes are drawn mutually perpendicular through a common origin O, with distances measured in the chosen unit.
Every pair of axes defines a plane: XY, YZ and ZX -- three flat walls through the origin.
The three planes slice space into eight octants, mirroring how two axes cut a plane into four quadrants.

concepts.title: Coordinates of a Point in Space and Sign Patterns
concepts.definition: A point in space carries a triple (x, y, z): walk x units along the x-axis, y along the y direction and z along the z direction. A point on an axis keeps two of its coordinates zero, a point on a coordinate plane keeps exactly one zero, and the sign pattern of the triple names the octant it lives in.
concepts.key_idea: Zeros localise the point -- two zeros means an axis, one zero means a coordinate plane, none means inside an octant.
concepts.textbook_ref: kemh111.txt lines 111-190 (section 11.3, coordinates of a point in space, points on axes and planes, octant sign patterns)

solution_steps.explain: The three entries of (x, y, z) record perpendicular distances from the three coordinate planes, taken with signs.
Two zero coordinates place the point on the remaining axis; a single zero places it on the coordinate plane of the other two axes.
The signs (+, -, +) for instance mark the fifth octant; all signs positive is the first octant, and each sign flip moves to a mirrored octant.

concepts.title: Distance Between Two Points in Space
concepts.definition: Extending the Pythagorean idea from the plane, the gap between points P(x1, y1, z1) and Q(x2, y2, z2) is the square root of the sum of the squared gaps in all three coordinates. The distance of a point from the origin is the same formula with the other point pinned at (0, 0, 0).
concepts.key_idea: Pythagoras applied twice -- once inside the horizontal plane, once lifting through the vertical -- gives the 3D distance.
concepts.textbook_ref: kemh111.txt lines 191-260 (section 11.4 distance between two points, formula derivation, distance from origin)

concepts.title: Midpoint and Section Ideas for Space Points
concepts.definition: Coordinate triples behave like ordered pairs under averaging: the point halfway between two space points simply averages each coordinate. This averaging view lets you test symmetric placements -- for example checking whether the origin is the centre of a segment -- before the full section formula arrives in class 12.
concepts.key_idea: Averaging coordinates coordinate-wise gives the halfway point of any segment in space.
concepts.textbook_ref: kemh111.txt lines 111-190 and 260-300 (section 11.3 examples with triples; worked placements relative to origin and axes)
question_patterns: find the midpoint of the segment joining two space points

solution_steps.explain: Match first with first, second with second, third with third across the two triples.
Each coordinate of the midpoint is the arithmetic mean of the corresponding coordinates of the endpoints.
Reflecting through a coordinate plane flips one coordinate's sign; through an axis, two signs flip -- these checks settle mirror questions instantly.
